topic: The Changing Role of Teachers in AI-Supported Education
text:
The growing use of artificial intelligence has created concerns that teachers may eventually be replaced by machines. However, AI is more likely to transform the teaching profession than eliminate it. As automated systems take over selected instructional and administrative tasks, teachers may devote more attention to guidance, classroom relationships, critical thinking, and student development.

AI can reduce the time teachers spend on repetitive work. Digital tools may assist with preparing quizzes, organising lesson materials, tracking attendance, and marking objective assessments. By automating part of this workload, schools can allow teachers to focus on activities that require professional judgement, such as explaining difficult concepts, supporting struggling students, and designing meaningful learning experiences.

The teacher’s role may also shift from being the main source of information to becoming a facilitator of learning. Students can now access explanations, summaries, and examples through AI systems at any time. Consequently, teachers must help students evaluate information, question unreliable outputs, and connect knowledge across different contexts. Teaching students how to use AI responsibly may become as important as teaching them how to search the internet.

Nevertheless, AI may create new pressures. Teachers must learn unfamiliar technologies, monitor inappropriate use, and redesign assessments that can still measure genuine understanding. Schools that introduce AI without sufficient training may increase teacher workload rather than reduce it. Furthermore, educators must remain accountable for decisions that affect students, even when those decisions are supported by automated systems.

AI does not remove the need for teachers; instead, it increases the importance of distinctly human abilities. Empathy, professional judgement, encouragement, and ethical responsibility cannot be fully automated. The future teacher will need both educational expertise and AI literacy, using technology as an assistant while retaining responsibility for the learning process.
